summary: This PR refactors the rule configuration system to use a unified flat list format. Instead of having rules split into separate `current`, `increment`, and `manifest_comparisons` buckets, rules are now declared as a single list and automatically categorized by their base class. This simplifies configuration while maintaining backwards compatibility through auto-detection.

steps.title: New unified rule base classes
steps.narrative: The refactor starts with consolidating the rule type hierarchy. The new `SingleVersionRule` and `ComparisonRule` base classes replace the old fragmented system, providing a clean foundation for auto-detection. Notice how both inherit from a common `Rule` base with standardized initialization and hashing behavior. This unified approach eliminates the need for separate `ConfigurableSingleVersionRule` and complex type protocols.

refs.heading: Validation Rules
refs.excerpt: Rules are defined as a flat list. Vertagus automatically detects whether each rule validates a single version (e.g., format checks) or compares versions (e.g., increment checks).

steps.title: Unified rule registry and auto-detection
steps.narrative: With the new base classes in place, we can build a unified registry that loads rules from both libraries and automatically categorizes them. The `get_rule_category()` function uses isinstance checks against the base classes to determine whether a rule handles single-version validation or version comparisons. This eliminates the need for manual categorization in configuration files.

refs.heading: Validation Rules > Built-in Rules
refs.excerpt: The output of this command will be a list of rules, their descriptions, and their type (`single_version` for format validation rules, `comparison` for rules that compare the current version to a previous version).

steps.title: Flat configuration data model
steps.narrative: The configuration types are dramatically simplified. Instead of the nested `RulesConfig` with separate `current`, `increment`, and `manifest_comparisons` sections, we now have `RulesConfig = list[Union[str, TypeAndConfig]]`. This allows rules to be expressed as either simple strings or objects with type/config pairs, all in one flat list. The `RulesData` dataclass follows suit with a single `rules` field.

refs.heading: Validation Rules
refs.excerpt: Configurable rules are rules that accept configuration values. To use a configurable rule, list it as an object with `type` and `config` fields.

steps.title: Rule parsing and categorization factory
steps.narrative: The heart of the new system is `create_rules()` which takes a flat list of rule items and returns three categorized lists. Each rule item can be a string (rule name) or dict (with type/config), gets instantiated from the registry, then sorted into single-version, comparison, or manifest-comparison buckets based on isinstance checks. This handles the complexity behind the scenes while keeping configuration simple.

refs.heading: Validation Rules > Built-in Rules
refs.excerpt: The output of this command will be a list of rules, their descriptions, and their type (`single_version` for format validation rules, `comparison` for rules that compare the current version to a previous version).

refs.heading: Validation Rules > Configurable rules
refs.excerpt: Configurable rules are rules that accept configuration values. To use a configurable rule, list it as an object with `type` and `config` fields.

steps.title: Updated documentation and examples
steps.narrative: The configuration docs now showcase the simplified flat rule format. Project rules are shown as a simple list mixing built-in rules like `not_empty` and `any_increment` with configurable rules using the `{type, config}` syntax. Stage rules follow the same pattern. The examples demonstrate how much cleaner this is compared to the old nested structure while maintaining the same functionality.

refs.heading: Project Section
refs.excerpt:
The `project` section defines versioning rules and stages:

```yaml
project:
  rules:
    - not_empty             # Validates current version is not empty
    - regex_mmp             # Validates current version matches semver format

steps.title: Updated list-rules command output
steps.narrative: The `vertagus list-rules` command now uses the unified registry to show all available rules in a single table with auto-detected categories. Instead of separate queries to single-version and comparison rule loaders, it calls `get_all_rules()` and uses `get_rule_category()` to determine the type column. This provides a cleaner user experience while leveraging the new unified system.

refs.heading: `vertagus list-rules`
refs.excerpt:
### `vertagus list-rules`

Display all available validation rules.

```bash
vertagus list-rules
```
